questions.question: A shopkeeper kept the marked price of an item at Rs. 500. He sold it at a scheme discount of 10% and 20% and got a profit of 25%. What was the cost price of the item?

Discounts = 10% and 20%

Profit = 25%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 - Discount1) × (1 - Discount2)

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit)

**Calculation:**

SP = 500 × (1 - 0.10) × (1 - 0.20)

⇒ SP = 500 × 0.90 × 0.80

⇒ SP = 500 × 0.72

⇒ SP = ₹360

CP = 360 / (1 + 0.25)

⇒ CP = 360 / 1.25

⇒ CP = ₹288

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper increases the selling price of an article by 15%. After increasing the selling price, he noticed that the profit percentage changed from 5% to 15%. The percentage increase in the cost price is:
questions.solution:

Profit percentage change = 5% to 15%

Let the initial SP be 100, then later SP will be 115 (increased by 15%)

⇒ New SP = (100 + 5)/100 × 100 = 105/100 × 100 = 105

Now on initial SP, he got 5% profit, 

⇒ 5% profit = 5/100 = 1/20

Initial SP = 1 + 20 = 21 units, Initial CP = 20 units

We have assumed that initial SP as 100, 

⇒ 21 units = 100 

⇒ 1 unit = 100/21 

Initial CP = 20 units = 20 × 100/21 = 20/21 × 100

For later he noticed 15% profit, 

⇒ 15% profit = 15/100 = 3/20

Later SP = 3 + 20 = 23, Later CP = 20 

Later SP is 115 as we have assumed, 

⇒ 23 units = 115

⇒ 1 unit = 115/23 = 5,

Later CP = 20 units = 20 × 5 = 100 

Percent change in CP, 

⇒ [(100 - 20/21 × 100)/20/21 × 100] × 100

⇒ [({{21over21} × 100} - {{20 over 21} × 100})/({20 over 21} × 100)] × 100

⇒ {{{100 over 21} (21- 20)} over {{20 over 21} times 100}} times 100

⇒ {1 over 20} times 100 = 5%

**∴ The percent in the CP is 5%.**

questions.question: What will be the actual profit percentage (rounded off to nearest integer) after selling an article at a certain price, while there occurs a loss of 45% on selling the article at (3)/(8) of the selling price?

A loss of 45% on selling the article at (3)/(8) of the selling price

Loss = CP - SP

SP = CP x (100 - loss)/100

As there is a loss of 45% on selling article at 3/8 of the SP

as the product is sold at 3/8 of the SP

⇒ **Hence, The actual profit is 47%.**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 35% more than its cost price. If a discount of 15% is given, what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price (MP) is 35% more than the cost price (CP).

Discount given is 15%.

**Formula Used:**

Profit Percentage (Profit%) = (Selling Price - Cost Price)/(Cost Price) times 100

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) - Discount

Marked Price (MP) = Cost Price (CP) + 35% of Cost Price (CP)

Discount = 15% of Marked Price (MP)

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Marked Price (MP) = CP + 35% of CP

⇒ MP = 100 + 35% of 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 35

⇒ MP = 135 units

Discount = 15% of MP

⇒ Discount = 15% of 135

⇒ Discount = 0.15 × 135

⇒ Discount = 20.25 units

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount

⇒ SP = 135 - 20.25

⇒ SP = 114.75 units

Profit% = (SP - CP)/(CP) times 100

⇒ Profit% = (114.75 - 100)/(100) times 100

⇒ Profit% = (14.75)/(100) times 100

⇒ Profit% = 14.75%

**The profit percentage is 14.75% i.e. 14 (3)/(4)%.**

questions.question: Satish bought 35 notebooks for Rs. 700 and sold 28 of them for Rs. 600. Find his percentage gain.

50/7% = 7 1/7%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/830af17c2054e60ca84987afc55e9235e37207eed82932624acbd268a74461cd.png]

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 150/7 − 20

⇒ Profit = (150 − 140) ÷ 7 = ₹10/7

⇒ Gain % = [(10/7) ÷ 20] × 100

⇒ Gain % = (10 ÷ 140) × 100

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Fundamentals

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Gain = SP − CP. Loss occurs when CP > SP. Loss = CP − SP.

Percentage Calculations

Gain% = (Gain/CP) × 100. Loss% = (Loss/CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.
